elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (1): "HDI warrants that (1) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — affirmative vendor warranty, not a mere covenant.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (2): "the Site and all software and other deliverables provided by HDI will conform in all material respects to their documentation."

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (2) opens "for twelve (12) months after delivery", attaching a 12-month period to the conformance warranty for the Site, software and deliverables.
Inserted clause (1): "such warranty shall apply for ninety (90) days after performance" — 90-day duration expressly tied to the workmanlike-performance warranty.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Remedy sentence: "The Company's remedy for breach of this Section 9(c) is, at HDI's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or refund..."
Remedy sentence includes "refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services, software or deliverable"; vendor-option structure matches the playbook model language.

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (3): "the Services and the Site will comply with all applicable laws" — broader than §7.2, which the rationale notes is confined to advertising.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (4): "the Services, the Site and all such software and deliverables will contain no viruses or other malicious code."

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Twelve-month conformance warranty in clause (2) exceeds the 90-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: Ninety-day workmanlike-performance warranty in clause (1) exceeds the 30-day fallback floor.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: Same remedy sentence: "re-performance, repair or replacement" available for breach of the inserted warranty.
Same remedy sentence: "refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services, software or deliverable."

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: the inserted paragraph delivers all eight preferred elements in operative language (workmanlike Services warranty with a 90-day period, 12-month documentation-conformance warranty for the Site/software/deliverables, compliance with applicable laws, no malicious code, and a re-performance/repair-or-replacement/refund remedy). The fallback floors are met a fortiori.

Deviation classification is correct: original §9 contains only mutual authority representations (9(a)) and the Globix acknowledgement (9(b)); there is no express performance or conformance warranty, no period and no remedy, so insertion rather than amendment is the right operation. Because the document contains no 'AS IS'/merchantability disclaimer, no disclaimer carve-out sentence is needed and none was added — correctly minimal.

Labeling cleanup (non-blocking but should be fixed in operative text): the inserted paragraph carries no subsection designator, yet its remedy sentence cross-references 'this Section 9(c)'. Add '(c)' at the start of the inserted paragraph so the internal cross-reference resolves to a labeled subsection.

Defined-term check: the insertion uses the capitalized term 'Services', which does not appear among the resolved definitions. Confirm 'Services' is defined elsewhere; if not, either define it in the insertion (e.g., 'the services described in Article 1 (the "Services")') or refer directly to HDI's Article 1 design, development, implementation, operation, maintenance and hosting obligations, so the warranty trigger is not left undefined.

Intent preserved: 9(a) and 9(b) are untouched, §1.6's late-delivery termination right and §7.2's advertising compliance covenant are unaffected and not contradicted, and no requirement outside the WARRANTY checklist (e.g., IP indemnity, SLA credits, uncapped damages) was smuggled in. Optional, out-of-checklist consideration only: 'The Company's remedy ... is' could be read as an exclusive remedy; if that concerns us, a short 'without limiting the Company's other rights and remedies' could be added, but it is not required for position completeness.
Margin comment is compliant in tone and content: it states what changed, cites the playbook preferred position and offers the 90-day/30-day fallback, without lecturing.
